decisions.reason: As a newly launched dietary supplement range with its own page and strong fit to the firm's consumer-health expansion, it is likely to be retained.
This skin and hair supplement was actively promoted at launch and fits the firm's adjacent OTC and pharmacy-focused portfolio, so management would likely continue it.
The joint-health supplement is somewhat less prominently presented than A and B but still sits close to the firm's established offer and should remain on the market.

The mushroom-based immune supplement is a more niche consumer-health product with weaker website prominence, raising exit risk, but it still supports portfolio broadening and is more likely kept than dropped.

Because this generic blood pressure product had an early quality-related problem on the website and is described as more distant from the firm's established offer, management would be relatively likely to discontinue it rather than keep investing in it.
